name: Vibration motor module (DFR0440)
description: Coin vibration motor on a small board with its own NPN transistor driver (8050 transistor, 1 kΩ base resistor, 10 kΩ pull-down, 1N4148 flyback diode, 10 Ω series resistor). The motor runs from the 5 V VCC pin; the Signal pin only switches the transistor, so a 3.3 V GPIO can drive it. High = vibrate, low or unconnected = off; PWM on Signal sets the strength. Sold as: DFRobot Gravity Vibration Motor Module (DFR0440), 3-pin Gravity connector Signal, VCC, GND.
eli5: A tiny buzzing motor like the one in a phone: set the pin high and it shakes, set it low and it stops.

pins.name: Signal
pins.description: Control input: high (3.3–5 V) = vibrate, low = off; PWM sets the strength. Drives the transistor base through 1 kΩ (about 2.5 mA from a 3.3 V GPIO); 10 kΩ pull-down keeps the motor off when unconnected.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Motor supply, 5 V (connect to the board's 5 V / VBUS pin, not 3.3 V)

supplierQuery: DFRobot DFR0440 Gravity vibration motor module
buildNotes: Wire VCC to 5 V (ESP32 VIN/5V, Pico VBUS), GND to GND and Signal to any GPIO. The motor current comes from VCC through the on-board transistor, never from the GPIO.
The board has a 2 mm PH2.0 Gravity socket; use the Gravity-to-Dupont cable that comes with it to reach a breadboard (green = Signal, red = VCC, black = GND).
High = vibrate, low = off. For gentler buzzing use PWM on Signal (e.g. machine.PWM at 1 kHz with a lower duty); very low duty may not start the motor.
The on-board 1N4148 flyback diode protects the transistor from the motor's back-EMF, so no extra diode is needed.
The motor draws tens of mA at 5 V and its brushes make electrical noise: power it from the 5 V rail and keep it away from analog sensor wiring.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

motor = Pin({SIGNAL}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # Signal high = vibrate
while True:
    motor.value(1)
    print('VIBRATE ON')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.value(0)
    print('VIBRATE OFF')
    time.sleep(2)

test.title: The motor switches on, then off again
